summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by chronic marginal (gastrojejunal) ulcer and post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring continuous gastrostomy tube feeds was admitted for recurrent severe epigastric and deep G-tube–site pain that worsened after an outpatient G-tube exchange and difficulty obtaining liquid oxycodone. Initial evaluation showed stable vital signs, normal labs, and chest radiograph without free air. CT abdomen with contrast confirmed the G-tube balloon in the gastric fundus with inflammatory changes at the abdominal wall insertion site but no hematoma, abscess, or discrete collection. Pain improved with medical management including liquid oxycodone and acetaminophen while continuing lansoprazole and sucralfate and maintaining continuous tube feeds with glucose monitoring. During the stay she developed asymptomatic hypotension felt related to atenolol and relative hypovolemia; atenolol was stopped and fluids given with improvement. She was discharged home ambulatory with a two-week supply of oxycodone, instructions to avoid NSAIDs, continue tube feeds and ulcer therapy, and follow up with her PCP and surgical/pain teams.
problems: Chronic gastrojejunal ulcer without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Personal history of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus
